observationsNotFindings: This artifact is a thin extraction and its validity is contingent on the parent's standing rather than self-contained. It carries no head, no file08Pin and no requiredNowUnchanged of its own; those live on core-gate-harness-specifications.v3, which I verified carries all three correctly and consistently with this cycle's dispatch. That is a legitimate structure for an extraction whose stated function is to occupy the D-086-promised artifactPathWhenAuthored, and the file says as much - 'The parent is the review subject' - but it does mean this ACCEPT rests on the parent's independent ACCEPT, which is itself one reviewer's and not yet D-000-recorded. If the parent is ever superseded, every extraction beneath it needs re-pinning, and there are five: DR-G01 through DR-G05.

The 83886080 handling is the sharpest thing in the file and worth naming positively. The constant is 80 MiB in bytes, which is exactly the conversion D-006 has not authorized - the parent's d006UnitStanding records byteMeaning as UNDECIDED because D-006 does not define MB as 1e6 or 2^20. Rather than quietly adopting one reading, the specification names the constant twice solely to refuse it and defers the size comparison to a later D-006 unit-and-accounting successor. A corpus that had simply written the byte count would have decided a product question by arithmetic.

Live DR-101 is OPEN and the live DR-G02 row's assurance cell reads SPECIFIED with status OPEN. The subject changes neither, and its registerRow DR-101 matches the parent's, so the extraction sits on the same row as its source.
